scenes.tts: The ferret shows that a progenitor's menu changes with time. But what actually changes inside the cell?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Clock in the Fly. A progenitor with a shrinking menu and a question mark inside it.
scenes.narration: The ferret shows that a progenitor's menu changes with time. But what actually changes inside the cell?

scenes.tts: The fly asks it in the cleanest form. Each half-segment of its nerve cord has about thirty neuroblasts.
scenes.caption: The fly asks it in the cleanest form. Each half-segment of its nerve cord has about 30 neuroblasts.
scenes.visual: Drosophila embryo nerve cord; one half-segment with about 30 identified neuroblasts.
scenes.narration: The fly asks it in the cleanest form. Each half-segment of its nerve cord has about 30 neuroblasts.

scenes.tts: Each neuroblast buds off ganglion mother cells, one after another. Each of those divides into neurons or glia.
scenes.visual: Successive snapshots of the same self-renewing neuroblast. At each, it buds one separate small ganglion mother cell, connected only to the neuroblast; each ganglion mother cell then splits into two daughters. Ganglion mother cells are not connected to one another.
scenes.narration: Each neuroblast buds off ganglion mother cells, one after another. Each of those divides into neurons or glia.

scenes.tts: In two thousand one, Takako Isshiki, Bret Pearson, Scott Holbrook and Chris Doe found a clock of transcription factors.
scenes.caption: In 2001, Takako Isshiki, Bret Pearson, Scott Holbrook and Chris Doe found a clock of transcription factors.
scenes.visual: Credit: Isshiki, Pearson, Holbrook and Doe, 2001. A clock face with four coloured sectors.
scenes.narration: In 2001, Takako Isshiki, Bret Pearson, Scott Holbrook and Chris Doe found a clock of transcription factors.

scenes.tts: Most neuroblasts switch on four factors in turn. Hunchback, then Kruppel, then P D M, then Castor.
scenes.caption: Most neuroblasts switch on four factors in turn. Hunchback, then Krüppel, then Pdm, then Castor.
scenes.visual: Coloured bands Hb, Kr, Pdm, Cas slide past the neuroblast in order.
scenes.narration: Most neuroblasts switch on four factors in turn. Hunchback, then Krüppel, then Pdm, then Castor.

scenes.tts: A ganglion mother cell keeps the factor that was on when it budded off. So do its neurons.
scenes.visual: Each budded ganglion mother cell keeps the colour of the band present at its birth; its two neurons share it.
scenes.narration: A ganglion mother cell keeps the factor that was on when it budded off. So do its neurons.

scenes.tts: The windows overlap, so the sequence is an outline, not a set of sharp steps.
scenes.visual: The coloured bands drawn overlapping at their edges. Label: overlapping windows.
scenes.narration: The windows overlap, so the sequence is an outline, not a set of sharp steps.

scenes.tts: One lineage makes this concrete. The neuroblast N B seven-one makes its first five motor neurons, U one to U five, in that order.
scenes.caption: One lineage makes this concrete. The neuroblast NB7-1 makes its first five motor neurons, U1 to U5, in that order.
scenes.visual: NB7-1 labelled; five motor neurons U1 to U5 appear in birth order.
scenes.narration: One lineage makes this concrete. The neuroblast NB7-1 makes its first five motor neurons, U1 to U5, in that order.

scenes.tts: In this idealized picture, U one and U two come in the Hunchback window, and U three with Kruppel. U four comes with P D M alone. U five needs P D M and Castor together.
scenes.caption: In this idealized picture, U1 and U2 come in the Hunchback window, and U3 with Krüppel. U4 comes with Pdm alone. U5 needs Pdm and Castor together.
scenes.visual: Each U neuron coloured by its window: U1, U2 Hunchback; U3 Krüppel; U4 Pdm only; U5 striped in both Pdm and Castor colours. Label: idealized; windows overlap.
scenes.narration: In this idealized picture, U1 and U2 come in the Hunchback window, and U3 with Krüppel. U4 comes with Pdm alone. U5 needs Pdm and Castor together.

scenes.tts: Now read a grid. Rows are place, which neuroblast. Columns are time, which window.
scenes.visual: Place-by-time grid: rows NB7-1 and another neuroblast (labelled schematic); columns Hb, Kr, Pdm without Cas, Pdm + Cas. NB7-1 row filled U1 U2, U3, U4, U5; schematic row: different, unnamed neurons.
scenes.narration: Now read a grid. Rows are place, which neuroblast. Columns are time, which window.

scenes.tts: The same factor gives a different neuron in a different row.
scenes.visual: The Hb column highlighted top to bottom: different neurons in each row.
scenes.narration: The same factor gives a different neuron in a different row.

scenes.tts: But expression in sequence is only a correlation. To show the factors set identity, take one away, or keep it on too long.
scenes.visual: Genotype table appears: Hunchback normal; removed; kept on.
scenes.narration: But expression in sequence is only a correlation. To show the factors set identity, take one away, or keep it on too long.

scenes.tts: Hunchback and Kruppel also pattern the early embryo. So the tests changed them in the nervous system itself.
scenes.caption: Hunchback and Krüppel also pattern the early embryo. So the tests changed them in the nervous system itself.
scenes.visual: Small inset: early embryo with gap-gene stripes; then focus on the nerve cord only.
scenes.narration: Hunchback and Krüppel also pattern the early embryo. So the tests changed them in the nervous system itself.

scenes.tts: Without Hunchback in the nervous system, first-born identities were lost in the lineages examined.
scenes.visual: Row 'removed' fills: first-born identities lost (in the lineages examined).
scenes.narration: Without Hunchback in the nervous system, first-born identities were lost in the lineages examined.

scenes.tts: Predict. Keep Hunchback on long after it would switch off. Do the extra cells look early-born or late-born? And of which lineage?
scenes.visual: Row 'kept on' shows a question mark. Predict card: early or late? which lineage?
scenes.narration: Predict. Keep Hunchback on long after it would switch off. Do the extra cells look early-born or late-born? And of which lineage?

scenes.tts: The lineages made extra cells with first-born features. In N B seven-one, extra cells resembled U one or U two.
scenes.caption: The lineages made extra cells with first-born features. In NB7-1, extra cells resembled U1 or U2.
scenes.visual: Row 'kept on' fills: extra first-born-like cells. NB7-1 lineage shows extra U1/U2-like cells.
scenes.narration: The lineages made extra cells with first-born features. In NB7-1, extra cells resembled U1 or U2.

scenes.tts: Each lineage made its own first-born type. Hunchback did not make every first-born cell the same.
scenes.visual: Back to the grid: extra cells appear in the Hb column of each row, each a different type.
scenes.narration: Each lineage made its own first-born type. Hunchback did not make every first-born cell the same.

scenes.tts: Prolonged Kruppel made extra second-born cells.
scenes.caption: Prolonged Krüppel made extra second-born cells.
scenes.visual: Extra row: Krüppel kept on, extra second-born cells.
scenes.narration: Prolonged Krüppel made extra second-born cells.

scenes.tts: In two thousand six, the same laboratory showed that P D M and Castor specify U four and U five.
scenes.caption: In two thousand six, the same laboratory showed that P D M and Castor specify U four and U five.
scenes.visual: Credit: Doe laboratory, 2006. U4 highlighted in the Pdm colour; U5 in Pdm and Castor colours together.
scenes.narration: In two thousand six, the same laboratory showed that P D M and Castor specify U four and U five.

scenes.tts: Birth order had become a genetic program that could be broken and rewired.
scenes.visual: The clock face with a wrench beside it. Label: break it, prolong it.
scenes.narration: Birth order had become a genetic program that could be broken and rewired.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: place picks the class of neuron. Time, read as a cascade of factors, picks the member within it.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card over the grid: row = place picks the class; column = time picks the member.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: place picks the class of neuron. Time, read as a cascade of factors, picks the member within it.
